title: Connect-volume seed: prioritize device-reported / last-known volume over fixed default
why: Alec (2026-07-29): the connect seed today always uses a fixed connect-default (35%) on a user-initiated connect, a holdover from when the seed inherited the Macs system volume and could blast the user. He wants the priority reordered: (1) the device/system own reported current volume if available, (2) otherwise the level that device previously had in our system, persisted per device across restarts, (3) the fixed connect-default only as a last resort for a never-seen device. Only the user-connect branch changes; F-REBIND (out-of-band reconnect) already preserves the in-session level and is untouched.
what: Read-only research + plan: docs/plans/PLAN-CONNECT-VOLUME-SEED.md. Traces the current seed (NativeBackend.connectVolumeSeed, userConnectSeed, stashedVolume, known[id].volume), the wire/UI domain conversion setSpeakerVolume already demonstrates for a receiver-reported level, and the vendored AirPlay sender/receiver protocol. Feasibility verdict: no GET_PARAMETER or any pull primitive exists anywhere in the vendored C sender (0 matches); the sender is the protocols volume authority and only ever pushes SET_PARAMETER. The only receiver-volume signal is an asynchronous, receiver-initiated push (RTSP reverse /event channel or DACP setproperty, both already wired to NativeBackend), coded and documented as a change notification, not an initial-state announcement; whether any receiver fires one unprompted at connect time, early enough to beat the seeds own push, is unverified and needs a live hardware probe (T-I1). Persistence finding: known[id].volume and stashedVolume are in-memory only today, nothing is written to disk, so tier 2 (persisted last-known level) is new work, not a rename -- DeviceIconStore.swift is the direct pattern to copy (stable colon-hex device id, Codable versioned JSON, same Application Support directory). Also raises, without deciding, an anti-blast open question: a device reporting 100% reopens the exact blast risk the fixed default was built to close, so the plan proposes T-I2 as an owner decision between trusting tier 1 unclamped, a cheap ceiling clamp, or a genuine ramp. Task list separates investigation-remaining (T-I1 live protocol probe, T-I2 anti-blast decision) from implementation (T-F1 bounded-listen tier-1 mechanism, T-F2 DeviceVolumeStore, T-F3 write-through wiring, T-F4 rewire connectVolumeSeed, T-F5 tests, T-F6 docs), gated on the two owner decisions.

title: BT-mic (HFP) trigger causes app<->Bluetooth rebuild oscillation with audible drops
why: Reproduced live 2026-07-29 ~19:40 (telemetry sid C98DF1E0): triggering the Bluetooth microphone (HFP mode) while streaming caused a rebuild ping-pong — 16000Hz rebuild+session_reset at 19:40:01, 44100Hz rebuild+session_reset at 19:40:23, another device_change + rebuild 2s later with rebind_recover_flush noop_fallback. Each of our tap rebuilds touches the BT device mid-renegotiation, likely re-perturbing it (our private tap-aggregate includes the BT device as a whole sub-device, input side unrestricted — NativeCaptureCoordinator.swift createAggregate ~:2263 — so aggregate IO may itself engage the mic path and force/prolong HFP). Owner: big drop + back-and-forth disconnect between app and Bluetooth; not urgent but must be addressed.

TRIGGER (takes ~1 min, fully reliable): connect WH-1000XM3 as the Mac's system output, stream
whole-system audio to an AirPlay speaker (Sonos Move 2, C4:38:75:0E:BF:4A), then open the mic
(FaceTime / Voice Memos record / Photo Booth). The headset's OUTPUT device collapses
44100 -> 16000 on mic-open and recovers 16000 -> 44100 on mic-close (HFP hands-free), ~14 s apart.
NOTE: the headset exposes output and mic as SEPARATE CoreAudio devices (CC-98-8B-93-16-55:output /
:input); the :input device sits at 16000 permanently and is NOT the trigger. The OUTPUT device
collapsing is. Also note AudioObjectIDs are per-HAL-client: the app logged this device as 167 while
an external probe saw 107 - do not try to correlate raw IDs across processes.

MEASURED COST (new netDriftSeconds counter, landed on claude/cadence-counter-fix):
  before mic:  net 7.745, flat across 5 windows
  mic opens:   net 8.220  (+0.475 s)
  mic closes:  net 8.927  (+0.708 s)
  after:       net 8.927, flat across 8 windows
  => 1.18 s of audio lost per mic toggle, in two discrete jumps, nothing in between.
Each edge does aggregate_destroy + create_and_start + format_reconciled + a full AirPlay
session_reset(recovery=flush_first) + rebind + rebind_recover_flush. send_sched gap_max goes
11.9 ms -> 493.8 ms (open) and 563.8 ms (close).

SECOND DEFECT, arguably worse, found the same run: for the ENTIRE 16 kHz window the app follows the
device down and streams 16 kHz upsampled audio to the AirPlay speaker - transition logs
"16000/2 creatingTap -> capturing", format_reconciled {aggregateRate:16000, declaredRate:48000},
send_sched gap_p50 shifts 11.6 -> 20.0 ms for the whole window. So the speaker gets materially
degraded audio for as long as the mic is open, not just a gap at each edge. Fix direction: do not
adopt the output device's nominal rate as the capture rate when that rate is an HFP artifact
(16000 on a device that was 44100/48000 a moment ago is the marker). This is separate from the
rebuild cost and may be the more user-visible half.

THIRD, OPEN AND UNCAUSED - please investigate as part of this entry: playback volume audibly
INCREASES while the mic is active, and returns to normal when it closes (owner-reported, same run).
Channel count stays stereo throughout (16000/2), so mono-being-duplicated-into-both-channels is
RULED OUT. No cause established. Cheapest next step is an isolation test: play to the headset
WITHOUT routing through the app and open the mic - if it still gets louder it is macOS's HFP volume
curve and out of our hands; if it only happens through the app it is ours. Untested either way.

title: Same-device AirPlay handoff: yield the speaker instead of fighting for it
why: Live-found 2026-08-07 (Alec, handoff live test). Releasing the PTP ports is enough only when macOS wants a DIFFERENT speaker. title: Release telemetry: product analytics + post-release health monitoring
why: Every bug so far has been found by Alec testing live on his own Mac. Once the app is in other people's hands there is currently NO way to see how it is used or whether it is working: AudiouterCore/Sources/AudiouterCore/Telemetry.swift is a local-only diagnostic decision log (JSON lines under ~/Library/Logs/Audiouter/, categories permission/captureWS/capturePA/airplay/localPlayback/lifecycle, per docs/plans/PLAN-TELEMETRY-SYSTEM.md) that never leaves the machine and is written for an agent to grep after the fact, and the STABILITY(id) ledger is the same shape. Alec wants both halves: what users actually do (which surfaces, which device kinds, group vs single, per-app routing uptake) and whether the shipped build is healthy (crashes, capture/TCC failures, AirPlay bind failures, dropouts, judder) without waiting for someone to email him.
what:
Two deliverables, in order.

(1) DECISION BRIEF first, no code, into docs/plans/PLAN-RELEASE-TELEMETRY.md. It must settle, with Alec: (a) does the app phone home AT ALL, or is the shipping answer local-only with a user-initiated 'send diagnostics' export? (b) if it phones home: opt-in with a consent screen vs opt-out, and where the toggle lives (AudiouterCore/Sources/AudiouterSettingsUI/ — GeneralSettingsViewController or a new Privacy pane; consent also needs a slot in the onboarding/permission-priming flow, which already exists); (c) destination and vendor. HARD CONSTRAINT on (c): the repo is GPL-2.0-or-later (LICENSE, and every source file carries the SPDX header), so a proprietary closed-source analytics SDK linked into the app is a licensing conflict — candidates must be either a plain HTTPS POST we write ourselves (no dependency, the razor answer), or a GPL-compatible open-source client. Same licensing-boundary reasoning that put AirPlayEngine in its own package applies here. (d) the exact event schema and what is NEVER sent: no speaker names, no app bundle ids of what the user plays, no network identifiers, no IP-derived location — these are the fields that make the difference between 'usage counts' and 'a log of what you listen to and where you live'. (e) retention + a documented data-collection table Alec can transcribe into the App Store privacy nutrition label (he owns App Store Connect himself). (f) how it is neutralized in dev: it must be OFF under HeadlessRuntime.isActive and under AIRPLAY_BACKEND=mock, and must never fire from a dev/unsigned build, or Alec's own test builds pollute the data.

(2) BUILD what the brief settles. Reuse Telemetry.swift's proven shape rather than standing up a second system — static facade, off-thread serial queue, isEnabled fast-path, fails-safe (any error swallowed, never throws, never crashes the host), size-bounded, and MUST NOT be called from the real-time IOProc/render path. Realistically this is a new emit category plus a consent-gated uploader that batches from the existing on-disk file, not a parallel logger. Health signals should be derived from failure points that are ALREADY instrumented (permission gate divergence, capture state transitions, AirPlay bind/rebind/session-reset, tap rebuilds, the STABILITY(id) ledger) so the release-health half is mostly plumbing, not new instrumentation. Crash reporting is a separate question inside the brief: macOS already writes crash reports and, for a Developer-ID build, they can reach the developer via Apple's own channel — check that before building anything custom.

Scope fence: docs-only until Alec answers the brief. No network code, no consent UI, and no new dependency before that.
notes: 2026-08-08 Created from Alec's ask: tracking/telemetry for user behavior AND post-release health. Grounding checked at creation: Telemetry.swift exists and is local-only diagnostics (309 lines, docs/plans/PLAN-TELEMETRY-SYSTEM.md); docs/SPEC.md contains no privacy or analytics stance at all, so the brief has to write one; LICENSE is GPL-2.0 (the SDK constraint above is real, not hypothetical); Settings UI is AudiouterCore/Sources/AudiouterSettingsUI/. Blocking open question = (1)(a)+(b): phone home or not, opt-in or opt-out.

title: Alignment wizard needs its own tick source (works with music paused)
why: The wizards ticks are mixed into the CAPTURED system audio, so with nothing playing the tap delivers no buffers and no ticks sound at all — the user must start music before aligning, which Alec rejects as not how people think. Live-confirmed 2026-08-08; shipped as a known limitation in 004.
what: Give the wizard a paced PCM source feeding the SAME delivery tail (AirPlay engine write, synced-local sink, every BT sink) so all outputs render the identical tick through their own real delays. FIRST STEP: re-scope with the single-producer constraint STATED UP FRONT — do NOT reuse the earlier work order, which failed two spec-check rounds. WHY IT FAILED: its deliveryLock design had the RT thread try()-take a lock the tone source holds on a steady cadence; a miss drops a captured buffer, and because the sinks anchor ONCE then run as FIFOs, every drop permanently shifts that devices alignment — corrupting exactly what the wizard measures. THE NEXT DESIGN MUST BE SINGLE-PRODUCER BY CONSTRUCTION (e.g. route synthetic blocks through the same serial delivery path, or have the capture side PULL from the tone source, rather than two threads pushing behind a lock). Other landmines the checks surfaced: a THIRD test (AlignmentTickInjectorTests.swift:314-350 wizardModeSilencesTheMusicInTheSharedFeedAndManualDoesNot) asserts the replacesProgram behavior any such change removes; the tick mix at NativeCaptureCoordinator:1128-1130 sits OUTSIDE the proposed lock span and AlignmentTickInjector.cursor is lock-free-because-single-consumer, so a second injector writer must be avoided; SyncedLocalBaseResampler survives a skipped buffer but splices (audible click) and loses contiguity; keep the -47dBFS keep-alive bed + 3s wake preamble (Sonos Move power-gates its amp).

title: Routing to the Mac's own output: its slider doesn't change the volume, and should be its own level
why: Alec, live 2026-08-08: select ONLY the Mac (MacBook speakers / system out) in Audiouter and drag that row slider — the speakers do not get louder or quieter at any position. He also wants that level to be the Mac own independent fader, no longer mirrored to or from the macOS system volume (DECIDED, reading (a); Main stays the ceiling, sent is still Main x Group x Device).
what: Root cause is by construction — do not re-derive it. The Mac row writes NO hardware (NativeBackend.swift:2087, the localDeviceID branch of setSpeakerVolume): it only sets SyncedLocalSink gain via pushSyncedLocalGain. That sink exists ONLY when the Mac AND >=1 AirPlay device are selected (wantSyncedLocal = macSelected && !ids.isEmpty, NativeBackend.swift:2439). Mac-only selection therefore runs no capture and no sink — audio plays natively through macOS — so the slider has nothing in the signal path to act on. Today the ONLY writer of the Mac hardware level is setMasterGain mirrorToSystemVolume arm (Main). CRUX to settle before building: with no capture running, the macOS system volume is the only lever, so exactly one control must own that write — either the Mac row owns it (and Main mirror is retired or becomes Main x macRow) or some equivalent single-owner scheme. Two controls cannot both own one knob, and the 2087 comment says the no-hardware rule exists precisely to keep Main sole owner. SECOND, separate case: even Main mirror write silently no-ops on an output with no settable volume (the 029 public aggregate, plain HDMI) — PLAN-VOLUME-KEY-INTERCEPTION 0b. Its 2 says build that fold-Main-into-sink-gain half together with volume-key interception as ONE we-own-the-volume mode, and do NOT gate on systemOutputVolume == nil (a live session disproved that gate).

Referred to in 029's close as 'volume-dead-on-aggregate = the separate A2 interceptor work'; this is that entry, now with a live report behind it. Related: 014 (dropped, described the pre-decoupling mirror), 018 (connect seed), 026 (same-device handoff).

Reading (b) is REJECTED: Main stays the ceiling, sent level is still Main × Group × Device, the Mac row is just the device stage for the Mac. Do not re-ask this.

Do not spend a live session confirming the slider is dead in that state; spend it on the ownership decision in `what`.

title: Volume-key interception when the Audiouter aggregate is the default output
why: With the aggregate as the default output macOS kills the volume keys (crossed-out HUD) and greys every volume slider, so the only way to change volume while routing is to open the app. Settled 2026-08-07 by static analysis of ControlStrip.app: discrete Touch Bar Volume Up/Down post a real Consumer-page HID usage via _DFRFoundationPostHIDUsage and ARE interceptable; the Touch Bar/menu-bar/Control-Center sliders call _AudioObjectSetPropertyData directly and never can be. Virtual-driver alternative rejected by Alec (admin-password install).
what: Full plan in docs/plans/PLAN-VOLUME-KEY-INTERCEPTION.md (commit f4708272). One we-own-volume mode gated on default-output UID == AggregateOutputDevice.productUID (AggregateOutputDevice.swift:87) or systemOutputVolume == nil - never on capability flags, the aggregate advertises vmvc/scalarMain and lies. W1 mode predicate; W2 pure event decode (NSSystemDefined subtype 8, NX_KEYTYPE_SOUND_UP/DOWN/MUTE = 0/1/7) + macOS step math (1/16 per press, 1/64 with shift-option, snap to sixteenths); W3 CGEventTap shell (mask 1<<14, .defaultTap, head-insert, handle tapDisabledByTimeout) driving GroupController.applyExternalSystemVolume (GroupController.swift:846) and setMainOutMuted (:873); W4 syncedLocalGain (NativeBackend.swift:2025) folds Main in when the mode is on, else the Mac speakers stay at full while AirPlay drops, plus SystemOutputVolume.setVolume must report success so lastSeenSystemVolume stops memoing no-op writes; W5 Control Strip auto-swap/restore via CFPreferencesSetAppValue on com.apple.controlstrip (user-owned, no admin), crash-safe marker + do-not-clobber-user-edits check; W6 revoked-Accessibility UI (CGEvent.tapCreate returns nil without it - reuse RemoteControlPriming, SetupModel.swift:221); W7 live checklist. No HUD (Alec). Do not merge - hand back for live test.

Alec asked for it 2026-08-08 right after the full bar shipped and worked.
what: Step 1 (cheap, ~1h, do first): private /System/Library/PrivateFrameworks/OSD.framework - OSDManager, plus the OSDUIHelper XPC service on newer macOS. Draws the REAL system HUD; MonitorControl uses this route for external displays. Reported DEGRADING on recent macOS (percentage stops updating on Tahoe); macOS 27 unverified, so this is a spike not a plan - either free or a fast no. Wire either to TouchBarFullBar.onVolumeStep/onToggleMute and to VolumeKeyInterceptor so the keys get feedback too. NOTE Alec previously locked HUD=none for the interceptor (2026-07-26); that call predates the custom bar and should be re-confirmed.

title: Now-playing via mediaremote-adapter: real transport state, track metadata, and the playing app
why: Apple gated MediaRemote: on macOS 27 its symbols still resolve but MRMediaRemoteGetNowPlayingApplicationIsPlaying never calls back - probed, not assumed (dev/spikes/volume-key-tap/mrprobe.swift). So the custom Touch Bar play/pause glyph currently follows a PROXY (TouchBarFullBar.noteAudioLevel: our own captured audio RMS), which tracks audible output rather than transport state - a notification chime during a pause reads as playing. Beyond fixing the glyph this unlocks a real feature set: track title/artist/artwork, elapsed+duration, and crucially the BUNDLE ID of the app currently playing, which ties directly into per-app routing (lead with the active player instead of making users hunt a list).
what: Use ungive/mediaremote-adapter (BSD-3, compatible with our GPL-2.0-or-later WITH attribution + SPDX BSD headers on vendored files). DO NOT use ejbills/mediaremote-adapter - it has NO licence file, so its own additions are all-rights-reserved. Mechanism: /usr/bin/perl is Apple-signed and entitled, so the script loads a bundled MediaRemoteAdapter.framework (bundled, NOT linked) that streams now-playing to stdout: /usr/bin/perl <script> <framework> [<testclient>] COMMAND. Work: build framework via CMake; bundle+codesign script and framework in make-app.sh alongside ptp-helper/tcc-probe (inside-out, before the app); Swift wrapper supervising the subprocess with capped-backoff restart and clean kill on terminate; PURE parsing layer unit-tested against sample/malformed/truncated stdout (no test may spawn perl). MANDATORY graceful degradation: upstream ships a test command (exit 0 = functional) - on any failure fall back to the existing noteAudioLevel proxy, never crash/hang/block main. RISK: upstream warns of breaking API changes across minor revisions and was last tested on macOS 26; 27 is UNVERIFIED. Partial WIP exists uncommitted on branch claude/now-playing-mediaremote-adapter (NowPlayingMonitor.swift + vendor/) from a stopped agent - inspect before restarting.
